Then, scale every remaining value by a factor of 2. Finally, compute the mode of the remaining values (if several values tie for most frequent, choose the smallest).

Take all integers between 29 and 122, including both endpoints. First, discard every number that is 121 or greater. Then, retain only the values that are not multiples of 2. Finally, report how many numbers are left.

Take all integers between 41 and 189, including both endpoints. First, discard every number that does not have a 7 among its digits. Then, retain only the even integers. Then, add 1 to each remaining number. Finally, report how many numbers are left.
Consider the integers from 6 to 43, inclusive. First, discard every number that is 30 or greater. Of these numbers, give the largest remaining number.

Take all integers between 9 and 51, including both endpoints. First, discard every number that is 21 or smaller. Then, retain only the odd integers. Then, replace each remaining number x with 2 * x. Then, decrease every remaining value by 8. Of these numbers, compute the product of all remaining values modulo 72 (the non-negative remainder).

Take all integers between 34 and 46, including both endpoints. First, keep only the numbers that contain the digit 4. Next, discard every even number, keeping the odd ones. Next, replace each remaining number x with 4 * x. Finally, fold bitwise OR across the remaining values and give the result.
Consider the integers from 5 to 19, inclusive. First, keep only the numbers that are not divisible by 4. Finally, report the maximum of the remaining values.

Consider the integers from 7 to 48, inclusive. First, discard every number that is 14 or smaller. Next, replace each remaining number with its remainder modulo 14, taken in the range 0 to 13. Next, map every remaining value to the digit sum of its absolute value. Finally, compute the maximum minus the minimum over the remaining values.

Take all integers between 10 and 36, including both endpoints. First, keep only the numbers that are strictly less than 31. Next, keep only the numbers that are even. Then, replace every remaining value x with the digits of |x| written in reverse order, with the original sign restored and leading zeros dropped. Next, increase every remaining value by 6. Of these numbers, report the result of combining all remaining numbers with bitwise OR.
